recipe.prompt:
Write the personal line on a private dinner invitation from {{ sender.name | default: 'our team' }} to someone at {{ account.name }}.

The dinner: {{ defaults.headline }}. {{ defaults.subline }} No slides and no pitch. What the table talks about: {{ defaults.topic }} {{ defaults.topic_note }} The host is {{ defaults.host }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }}.

Inputs: account.name, account.industry and account.size_band describe the company. account.dossier.summary is our research summary. data.why_now is a recent reason to reach out and may be empty. data.invitee_title is the guest's job title and may be empty. Use facts from these inputs only. Never invent news, numbers, customers or people.

Return JSON with one key:
- why_you: one or two sentences, 40 to 280 characters, on why the guest from {{ account.name }} belongs at this table. Tie one specific fact about the company, data.why_now if there is one, to what the table will talk about, so it reads like the host wrote it after looking them up. Write to "you" or to the company. Never use a first name; the page adds the greeting. If the inputs hold no specific fact, say plainly that the table is for people who do their kind of work at a company this size, and stop. No flattery ("love what you are building", "impressive"), no "I noticed", "I saw" or "I came across", no question, no invitation to reply (the page has the RSVP).

Rules: no em dashes or en dashes. No exclamation marks. No email addresses or phone numbers. Never name other guests or say who else is coming. Plain words a person would say out loud to a peer; no marketing words.

recipe.rubric:
Grade data.why_you the way the guest reads it: the first lines of a printed invitation, right under the greeting. 10 is a line a busy operations leader reads once and feels was written for them.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- specific: it ties one fact about {{ account.name }} from the inputs to the table's topic. A line that only restates the company's name or industry scores 4 or lower.
- host_voice: it reads like the host wrote it by hand: plain, warm, short sentences, no pitch and no flattery.
- fits_page: it does not repeat the greeting, the date, the venue or the guest list, and it asks for nothing.
Answer yes or no:
- supported: is every claim about {{ account.name }} backed by the inputs below? Quote any that is not.
- weird_word: is there a phrase a person would not say out loud (jargon, marketing adjectives)? Quote it.
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, an exclamation mark, an email address or phone number, a first name, a question, a mention of other guests, a price.
Inputs: company {{ account.name }}, industry {{ account.industry | default: 'unknown' }}, size {{ account.size_band | default: 'unknown' }}. Research summary: {{ account.dossier.summary | default: 'none' }}. Recent reason: {{ data.why_now | default: 'none' }}. The table's topic: {{ defaults.topic }}
Pass when the overall score is 7.5 or higher, no 0 to 10 check is 6 or lower, supported is yes and weird_word is no. On a fail, name the check and quote the phrase to change. The fix never supplies replacement facts, names, numbers or customers.
